fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes after the 32-byte IVF header are passed to the decoder.
The frame size is clamped to the remaining input size, but the frame payload itself is attacker-controlled.
The attacker-controlled frame payload is passed to the AV1 decoder for parsing and reconstruction.

fine_trace.code: Tile data is parsed and decoded from the compressed bitstream.
fine_trace.note: The decoder parses tile headers and block data from the attacker-controlled bitstream, setting up tile dimensions and block parameters.

fine_trace.code: Block decoding iterates over mi_row and mi_col within the frame.
fine_trace.note: The decoder iterates over macroblock rows and columns, using attacker-controlled block sizes and partition types to determine the iteration bounds.

fine_trace.code: Block size is read from the bitstream and used to index into partition and transform tables.
fine_trace.note: The block size (bsize) is derived from attacker-controlled partition data and is used to index into arrays such as partition context and transform size tables.

fine_trace.code: Partition type is read from the bitstream and used to determine sub-block recursion.
fine_trace.note: The partition type is attacker-controlled and determines how the current block is subdivided, potentially leading to out-of-bounds reads when the partition type is inconsistent with the block size.

fine_trace.code: Partition is used to index into partition context arrays.
fine_trace.note: An invalid or inconsistent partition type for the given block size can cause an out-of-bounds read when indexing into partition-related lookup tables.

fine_trace.code: Sub-block recursion uses mi_row and mi_col offsets.
fine_trace.note: The recursion into sub-blocks uses attacker-controlled partition data to compute new mi_row and mi_col positions, which can exceed the frame dimensions and cause out-of-bounds reads in the mi grid.
When mi_row or mi_col exceeds the allocated mi grid dimensions due to inconsistent partition data, the read from mi_grid_visible goes out of bounds, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ.
